sections.category: AI security: Zscaler ships first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI, covering MCP channels, non-human identities, and endpoint AI threats

bullets.body: At its Zenith Live 2026 conference on June 9, Zscaler announced three new products it positions as the industry's first complete zero-trust platform for agentic AI. AI Broker sits inline on MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) channels, maintaining an Agent Registry that maps each agent's permitted data sources and enforces fine-grained access so no agent call traverses the network without policy approval. AI Access Graph, built on technology from the May 2026 $175 million acquisition of Symmetry Systems, maps how identities, applications, and data sources interconnect and enforces data-lineage policies in real time. Endpoint AI Security extends threat detection from cloud and server environments to employee browsers, extensions, plugins, and locally installed AI tools that conventional endpoint agents miss. On June 10, Oasis Security announced an integration that adds lifecycle governance for non-human identities and AI agents — discovery, ownership attribution, secret rotation, and inline enforcement — on top of the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange, delivering a unified control plane across machine-to-machine and agent-to-agent traffic. Together the launches address the enterprise gap between rapid agent deployment and identity-level security oversight.

sections.category: Agent platform: Databricks announces Agent Bricks and OpenSharing at Data + AI Summit, moving agentic infrastructure from experiment to production governance

bullets.body: On June 16, the second day of Databricks' Data + AI Summit, the company formally announced Agent Bricks, a developer platform for building, deploying, and governing AI agents in production. The platform organizes its capabilities into three pillars. Choice covers access to frontier proprietary models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi) and a new partnership with SpaceX to serve Grok natively, alongside support for LangGraph, Agno, CrewAI, Claude Code SDK, and OpenAI Agent SDKs; over 100,000 agents have already been built on the underlying infrastructure, processing more than one quadrillion tokens annually. Context adds MCP integration with Unity Catalog for scoped access to external data sources (Google Drive, JIRA, Slack, GitHub), a Genie Ontology layer for business semantics, an agent-memory service powered by Lakebase, and document-intelligence functions (ai_parse_document, ai_extract, ai_classify) for PDF and document processing. Control delivers Unity AI Gateway for unified governance across agents, models, and external tools, contextual security policies written in SQL, agent trace monitoring within the Lakehouse, and a Databricks Sandbox for isolated computing with scoped data access. Separately, Databricks and the Linux Foundation announced OpenSharing on June 10, an open vendor-neutral protocol that extends Delta Sharing to cover agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data, enabling zero-copy sharing of AI assets across organizations without proprietary marketplaces; founding partners include OpenAI, SAP, Stripe, Atlassian, and Amadeus.

sections.category: Inference engine: SGLang v0.5.13 ships Nemotron 3 Ultra and Cosmos 3 support with production-ready speculative decoding across triton, FA3, and MLA backends

bullets.body: SGLang released v0.5.13 on June 13 with model support for Nemotron 3 Ultra, Step-3.7-Flash, Command A+, and multiple diffusion models including Cosmos 3, LingBot-World, SANA-WM, and FLUX.2-Klein. The release promotes Spec V2 tree drafting with topk greater than 1 to production-ready status across the triton, FA3, MLA, and aiter backends, delivering improved speculative decoding performance at scale. Scheduler changes unify async value passing to reduce per-step overhead, and piecewise/breakable CUDA Graph coverage is extended to DSA models and DeepSeek V4. DeepSeek V4 enhancements include context parallelism, sparse-attention kernels, and MoE optimizations; SGLang-Diffusion adds real-time video generation with progressive resolution support. The release involved contributions from more than 70 developers. In broader context, SGLang already delivers roughly 29% higher throughput than vLLM on H100s (16,200 vs 12,500 tokens per second) and up to 6.4x gains on prefix-heavy workloads, and powers production deployments at xAI (Grok 3), Microsoft Azure, LinkedIn, and Cursor across approximately 400,000 GPUs.

sections.category: Anthropic Fable 5 export ban: senior technical staff dispatched to Washington in fast-moving negotiation to restore access to the suspended models

bullets.body: Anthropic's dispute with the US government over the June 12 export-control directive suspending Fable 5 and Mythos 5 escalated on June 15 as the company sent senior technical staff to Washington to pursue a negotiated resolution. The administration issued the directive after claiming awareness of a jailbreak technique; Anthropic's statement on its site identifies the specific concern as asking the model to read a codebase and fix software flaws — standard defensive security work that, as security researcher Katie Moussouris noted on June 16, is precisely the most valuable task an AI model can do for cyber defense, and that the same capability is present in competing systems like GPT-5.5. A live negotiation is moving unusually fast for Washington, with at least some officials signaling openness to a technical compromise, though as of June 16 both models remain offline for all customers globally while Anthropic works to restore access. Anthropic has stated that applying the same narrow-jailbreak-equals-recall standard across the industry would effectively halt all new frontier model deployments.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the Data + AI Summit continues through Wednesday and the Bay Area calendar fills with AI-security and dev/data events before the AI Engineer World's Fair opens June 29

bullets.body: The forward-looking calendar across all three sub-tracks for the coming weeks: Mainstream dev/data: the Databricks Data + AI Summit continues June 16-18 at Moscone in San Francisco (Day 2 today included Agent Bricks, OpenSharing, and agentic Unity Catalog updates); the AI Engineer World's Fair opens June 29-July 2 at Moscone West with dedicated Inference and Security tracks, 250-plus speakers, and a 12-track program. AI-security: AICamp hosts an invite-only AI Agent Security Documentary Premiere tonight, June 16 (6-9 PM PDT) at The Media Room, 582 Market St, San Francisco, with speakers including former White House CIO Theresa Payton and MIT's Ramesh Raskar; AI Tinkerers San Francisco presents an Offensive Security Demo Night on June 25 with live demos from local builders focused on agent attack surfaces; the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint (Linux Foundation and OPAQUE, confidential agents and secure AI workflows, 400-plus attendees expected); SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA's AI Summit is August 1-6 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas alongside DEF CON's AI Village; OWASP Global AppSec USA runs November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit global 2026 series (New York, London, APAC dates to be announced) remains on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is confirmed for July 23 at Moscone (Instinct/MI400-series focus expected); Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium; the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center. Further out, Snowflake Dev Day is June 25 in San Francisco; GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29; AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas.
